subject: Request: Temporary SLO adjustment for P1 latency during migration
messages:
From: Tina Morales <tina@finxcorp.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: support+finx_ticket@finxcorp.com, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finxcorp.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:23:00-08:00
Subject: Repeated P1 latency spikes — request for temporary SLO amendment

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this quickly. Over the past 48 hours we've seen multiple P1 incidents where token latency for our production inference calls spiked into the 2.4–3.1s range for short bursts (normal P1 median is ~300ms). The incidents align with your backend migration logs (INF-5821). Our legal/compliance team is concerned about hitting the SLO threshold and triggering a credit scenario while our product team has a go-live next week.

Can Redwood provide a temporary, dated SLO adjustment or formal exception that covers the migration window (Dec 1–3 UTC) with clear conditions (max per-burst duration, guardrails, and rollback triggers)? We need this in writing to present to FinX execs.

I've attached a short CSV export of our request/incident timestamps. Please let me know who will own the escalation and the exact wording we can share with our stakeholders.

Appreciate it,
Tina
Tina Morales
Head of Platform — FinX Corp

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (CSV, 12 rows)

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Repeated P1 latency spikes — request for temporary SLO amendment

Ben/Laura — forwarding FinX's ask. Key points:
- Repeated P1 latency spikes coincident with our INF-5821 migration traffic shaping.
- Customer requests a formal, timeboxed SLO exception (Dec 1–3 UTC) with defined guardrails.
- They need written approval to brief their execs.

Can we draft a minimal amendment (non-precedent-setting) that:
1) Grants a temporary relaxation on the P1 500ms target to a burst-aware SLA (e.g., accept up to X% of requests up to 3s during the window, with an upper cap on total minutes),
2) Includes required monitoring/alerts (auto rollback trigger if 10-minute sustained >3s),
3) States no automatic credit will be issued if the customer follows mitigations and we meet the rollback trigger conditions.

Ben — can you start the draft? Laura — want your sign-off on the wording before I send. I'll loop in Ethan for operational guardrails.

Thanks,
Chloe
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Repeated P1 latency spikes — request for temporary SLO amendment

Team — Draft below. I'm keeping it conservative and timeboxed. Please comment inline; I want to get this to FinX within the hour.

---- DRAFT AMENDMENT (v0.1) ----
Redwood will temporarily modify the P1 response-time SLO applicable to FinX Corp between 2027-12-01T00:00:00Z and 2027-12-03T23:59:59Z to account for known migration-related transient latency. During this window Redwood agrees that:
1) The P1 response-time SLO target of 500ms median will be relaxed such that brief bursts of elevated latency are allowable where no single 10-minute contiguous period has a median token latency exceeding 3 seconds.
2) If a sustained 10-minute median token latency > 3s is observed, Redwood will initiate a rollback of the migration or activate the contingency plan and notify FinX within 15 minutes.
3) No service credits will be automatically applied for latency events that meet the conditions in (1) and where the rollback/contingency practices in (2) are followed.
4) Redwood will provide an incident timeline and mitigation summary within 24 hours of the end of the window.

---- end draft ----

Ethan — can you confirm we have the monitoring/alert capability to guarantee the 15-minute notify and the 24-hour post-window report? Laura — are you OK with the no-credit conditional language? I didn't loop Legal yet — would prefer to keep the wording operational rather than contractual for this narrow window.

Ben
Senior Account Executive

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-01T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Repeated P1 latency spikes — request for temporary SLO amendment

Thanks Ben — clean draft. Two small edits and one condition from my side:

Edits:
- Replace 'median token latency' in (1) with '10-minute median' to be explicit.
- Add a clause that any changes to the amendment after issuance require written approval from a Redwood Director-level signatory.

Condition:
- We cannot promise 'no service credits' unilaterally. Legal will need to sign off, but for speed I'm OK to send this as a "temporary operational amendment" with a statement that credits will be evaluated per the standard SLA post-window and are subject to mutual review.

If no objections by 14:00 PST I'll approve sending the operational amendment, attach the incident timeline, and request FinX confirm acceptance. Ben/Chloe: please cc legal@redwood.ai on the outgoing.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success (EMEA & US)
Redwood Inference

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
To: Tina Morales <tina@finxcorp.com>, support+finx_ticket@finxcorp.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ethan_park@redwood.ai, legal@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-12-02T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated P1 latency spikes — temporary operational amendment (Dec 1–3)

Hi Tina / Carlos,

Thanks again for flagging this and for the timeline you sent. Per our internal review we've prepared a timeboxed operational amendment for the migration window. Key points below and attached as a short doc for your execs:

- Window: 2027-12-01T00:00:00Z through 2027-12-03T23:59:59Z.
- Operational change: P1 SLO (500ms target) will be observed with a burst-tolerant rule: allowed brief bursts where no single 10-minute median token latency exceeds 3.0s.
- Rollback trigger: Any sustained 10-minute median > 3.0s will cause Redwood to initiate rollback/contingency and notify FinX within 15 minutes.
- Post-window reporting: Redwood will deliver an incident timeline and mitigation summary within 24 hours after Dec 3.
- Credits: This is an operational amendment for the migration window. Service credits remain governed by the standard SLA and will be evaluated after the window; we will not apply automated credits for burst events that meet the rollback/contingency criteria outlined above.

Attachments: proposed_sla_amendment_v1.docx, incident_timeline.csv

Next steps: please reply to confirm FinX acceptance of the operational amendment and whether you want Legal to convert this into a short addendum. If we do not receive objections by 23:59Z on Dec 2 we'll treat the amendment as accepted for the stated window so we can proceed with mitigation coordination.

I'll keep the channel open for live updates; Ben will be primary commercial contact and Ethan will be on-call operational lead for the rollback if needed.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
